parties:
Benode Behari Mondal ----- Petitioner
Vs
Arabinda Sarder and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the plaintiff petitioner is against judgment and decree dated 16-3-94 passed by the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No.130 of 1993 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 29-4-1993 passed by the Assistant Judge, Batiagata, Khulna in Title Suit No.5 of 1988.

2. Petitioner as well as opposite party Nos. 7-9 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.374 of 1987 which was subsequently re-numbered as Title Suit No.5 of 1988 against the opposite party Nos. 1-6 for setting aside that decree dated 11-6-1991 passed in Rent Suit No.676 of 1941 and auction dated 16-9-1941 held in Rent Execution case No.827 of 1941 and for declaration that judgment and order dated 7-3-42 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.275 of 1941 and judgment in Miscellaneous Case No.178 of 1942 and judgment dated 26-5-42 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.69 of 1942 are illegal,void and not binding upon the plaintiffs and also for setting aside the same.

3. The case of the plainitiffs, in short, is that lands of CS Khatian No. 82 corresponding to SA Khatian No.116 originally belonged to Aviram Sarder and Rupchan Sarder and others and predecessors of the plaintiffs were bargaders under the said owners and their names were recorded as such bargaders in the CS Khatian. Their further case is that Aviram died leaving son Guru Charan Ram Kanta and Rup Chand died leaving sons Ram Krishna and Ram Charan and they settled the suit land on 17-5-1939 with Arjun, Fakir, Sanatan Jageswar and Chandra Kanta by accepting a Kabuliyat and since then the said tenants possessed the suit land and thereafter they died leaving the "plaintiffs as their heirs. Plaintiffs" further case is that on 1-11-86 defendants threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession from the suit land and hence they field Title Suit No. 78 of 1986 and defendants filed a written statement on 27-6-87 and disclosed that the suit lands were auction purchased by their predecessors on 16-9-1941. Therefore, they filed the present suit challenging the aforesaid auction sale and all other related proceedings upon which the defendants based their claim in the suit land.

4. Defendant Nos. 11-12and 14-16 contested the suit by filing separate written statements.

5. The case of the defendant Nos. 11 and 12 is that the suit land was auction sold in Rent Execution case No. 827 of 1941 for realisation of the decretal dues of the Rent Suit No. 676 of 1941 and auction purchased by their predecessors and thereafter one of the tenants Chandra Kanta Mondal filed Miscellaneous case No. 275 of 1941 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Khulna for setting aside the ex parte decree passed in the rent suit and that case was dismissed on 7-3-42 and thereafter he filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 69 of 1942 and the said appeal was also dismissed. Thereafter another tenant Jogeswar Mondal filed Misc. Case No. 178 of 1942 for setting aside the auction purchase and the said case was dismissed on contest on 15-2-42 and since then they along with defendant Nos.14-16 are in possession of the suit land. Case of the defendant Nos.14-16 is that they purchased 3.63 acres of land from Ram Krishna Sarder whose brother Ram Charan Sarder died leaving son Kanah Sarder who left the country for India and as such his share became vested property and they took lease of his share from vested property authority.

On consideration of the material evidence trial Court decreed the suit. Being aggrieved by the same some of the defendants preferred appeal and court of appeal below by the impugned judgment set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and remanded the case. Being aggrieved by the same one of the plaintiffs obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that court of appeal below acted illegally in not deciding the appeal on merit and shirking responsibility sent the case on remand to the trial Court on flimsy ground that certain documents have been considered without being marked as exhibits.

7. Mr. M Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite parties submitted that neither the trial Court nor the court of appeal below considered the real point at issue involved suit so he submitted that if the case is sent back to the court of appeal below there should be clear direction to decide the real point at issue namely, whether the suit at the instance of the heirs of the judgment debtors is maintainable in the failure of their predecessor's attempt to set aside the same before it contested proceedings.

It appears from the impugned judgment that court of appeal below found fault with the judgment of the trial Court regarding its finding about possession and also that the trial Court considered the materials of Lease case No.28 of 1976-77 without marking the same as exhibits.

<u>8. In this case there is no dispute that Arun and others predecessors of the plaintiffs took settlement of the suit land from Ram Charan and others by Kabuliyat dated 17-5-39 Ext.2. Plaintiffs claimed the suit land on the basis of the said settlement. On the other hand, defendants claimed that the suit land was auction sold on 16-9-1941 in Rent Execution case No.827 of 1941 and auction purchased by Ram Charan and others, the predecessors of some of the defendants. Ext Ka is the certified copy of the decree passed on 11-6-1941 in Rent Suit No.676 of 1941 filed by Ram Charan Sardar and others against Arjun Mondal and others. Ext. Kha is the certified copy of the sale certificate dated 26-11-1941 by which the said Ram Charan Sardar and others purchased the suit land. Ext. Kha (1) is the writ of delivery of possession by which possession was delivered to the said auction purchasers on 14-12-1941. Ext. Ga is the certified copy of case register of Mise-judicial case register which shows that Jageswar Mondal one of the tenants filed Miscellaneous Case No.178 on 28-5-42 under section 174(3) of the Bengal Tenancy Act for setting aside the sale held on 16-9-1941 in Rent Execution case No.827 of 1941 against Ram Charan Sarder and others and the said case was dismissed on contest on 15-2-43. Ext. Cha is the certified copy of the order in Misc. Case No.275 of 1941 filed by Chandra Mondal against Ram Charan Sarder and the said order shows that the Misc. Case was dismissed on contest with cost. Ext. Gha (1) is the certified copy of order passed in Misc. Appeal No.69 of 1942 filed by Chandra MondaI against Ram Charan Sarder which shows that the said Misc. Appeal was also dismissed on contest. Besides the aforesaid documents defendants also produced and proved certain other documents such as rent receipts, Ext Cha series and information slip, Ext Chha, Kabala Ext. Ka (1), certified copy of mutation khatian Ext. Kha (1) and Kha 1(1), rent receipts Ext Ga(1) series, certified copy of certain orders in Title Suit No. 78 of 1976, and vested property rent receipts. Court of appeal below did not at all consider the aforesaid documents along with oral evidence on record to decide whether plaintiffs' raiyati interest in the suit land still subsist or not. None of the courts below also considered the absence of payment of rent by the plaintiffs from the date of alleged auction upto the date of filing the suit and effect of the writ of delivery of possession Ext. Kha(1). The record of the vested property case could be marked Ext. by the appellate Court if any of the parties filed an application for accepting the same as additional evidence. Court of appeal below merely shirked its responsibility in deciding the appeal without at all looking into oral or documentary evidence on record. This kind of shirking responsibility is highly deprecable. Court of appeal below being the last court of fact should consider all materials on record and is at liberty either to affirm or set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court after assigning reasons therefor. Court of appeal below in this case having not done so, I find merit on the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.</u>

9. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost and the judgment and decree of the court of appeal below is set aside and the case is sent back to the court of appeal below to decide the appeal on merit in the light of the discussions and observations made above. Court of appeal below is directed to dispose of the appeal within 3(three) months from the date of receipt of the record.

The lower court records be sent down immediately.

End.

lawyer:
Mir Moklesur Rahman with Nasrin Parvin, Advocates -----For the Petitioners. 
No one-----For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Akbar Hossain Khan (Md) and another ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Md. Awlad Hossain Khan and another ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule calls in question the order dated 8-6-92 passed by the Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka allowing the application of opposite party No. 2 Sher Mohammad under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure setting aside the ex parte decree dated 28-9-89 passed in SCC Suit No. 157 of 1985 of the 1st Court of Assistant Judge and SCC Judge, Dhaka.

2. Short facts relevant for the disposal of this case are that, the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted a suit for eviction of the defendants in the 1st Court of Assistant Judge and SCC Judge, Dhaka being SCC Suit No. 157 of 1985, alleging, inter alia, that they are the 16 annas owners of the suit premises fully described in the schedule of the plaint. In course of time defendant No. 1 became a monthly tenant under them in respect of the suit premises, which is a shop, at a rental of Taka 200.00 only per month. Defendant-opposite party No. 1 paid rent to them for the suit premises upto the month of January, 1985 and thereafter he defaulted in paying rent and did not pay any further rent in spite of repeated demands by the plaintiffs. In this way defendant No. 1 became a habitual defaulter. It has been further alleged in the plaint that defendant No. 1 illegally inducted defendant No. 2 in the suit premises as a sub-lessee beyond the knowledge of the plaintiffs. Under such circumstances, the plaintiffs served notice upon the defendants under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act determining the tenancy and thereafter filed the suit for eviction of the defendants.

3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing two separate written statements. In the written statement defendant No. 1 admitted that he was a monthly tenant under the plaintiffs and he paid rent to them upto January, 1985 but thereafter he failed to pay rent due to financial constraints and under unpropitious circumstances he was compelled to sub-let the suit premises to defendant No. 2.

4. Case of defendant No. 2, as made out in his written statement, appears to be that one Abdul Habib Khan was the landlord of the suit property and Abdul Malek was the tenant under him. On the death of said Abdul Malek his wife Nazma Bibi alias Naju became the tenant under the aforesaid landlord. Subsequently the said NazuBibi sub-let the suit premises to him. Landlord Habib Khan thereafter filed Title Suit No. 338 of 1975 in the 6th Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for eviction of the said Nazu Bibi on the ground of default in payment of rent and the said suit was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 125 of 1985. Defendant No. 2 further contended that he was a monthly tenant under the said Habib Khan and he was never a tenant under the plaintiffs and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. After a series of adjournments, mostly at the instance of the defendants, the suit was eventually taken up for ex parte disposal in the absence of the defendant-petitioners. The learned SCC Judge by his judgment dated 28-9-89 decreed the suit on contest against defendant No. 1 and ex parte against defendant-petitioner No. 2. Against this ex parte decree dated 28-9-89 passed in SCC Suit No. 157 of 1985 defendant No. 2 filed an application under Order 9, rule 13, CPC for setting aside the ex parte decree passed on 28-9-89.

6. It was alleged in the application under Order 9, rule 13, CPC that at about the relevant time the defendant-petitioner had been ailing and there was no male member in the family to look after the case as a result of which the suit was decreed ex parte on 28-9-89 beyond his knowledge and due to circumstances beyond his control. This application under Order 9, rule 13 CPC, out of which Misc. Case No. 106 of 1989 arose, appears to have been filed on 16-11-89. It also appears from the record that defendant opposite party No. 2 did not file any application for condonation of delay under the appropriate provision of law at the time of filing the case under Order 9, rule 13 CPC and the learned Court has not also formally condoned the apparent delay in filing the case.

7. Mr Mir Moklesur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the learned Assistant Judge seriously erred in law in passing the impugned order completely ignoring the clear provision of Article 164 of the Limitation Act which provides that an application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC directed against the ex parte decree shall have to be filed within 30 days of the decree when summons was duly served upon the defendants and within 30 days from knowledge when summons was not duly served upon the defendants. The learned Advocate further submits that since in the instant case summons was duly served upon the defendants, including defendant opposite party No. 1, and the defendants duly made their appearance and filed written statements in the suit and obtained several adjournments for hearing, it is manifestly evident that Misc. Case No. 106 of 1986 is clearly barred by limitation and, as such, the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in aIlowing the application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC completely ignoring the question of limitation. The learned Advocate further submits that in Misc. Case No.106 of 1989 defendant petitioner examined 2 witnesses and the opposite parties examined 1 witness in support of their respective cases. The learned Advocate further submits that on misreading and non-reading of the material evidence on record the learned Assistant Judge allowed the miscellaneous case in a most casual and arbitrary manner, occasioning failure of justice.

8. None appears for the opposite parties.

<u>9. In this case it is an undisputed fact that summons was duly served upon the defendants whereupon they entered appearance in the suit and filed written statements. It is also clear from the evidence on record that subsequently defendant opposite party No. 2 failed to appear after 12-6-88 and took no further step following which the suit was decreed on 28-9-89 on contest against defendant No.1 and ex parte against defendant No. 2. It is also an admitted fact that the application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC, which gave rise to Miscellaneous Case No. 106 of 1989, was filed on 16-11-89. From this it is apparent that this application for setting aside the ex parte decree was filed after 49 days from the date of passing the impugned decree. Article 164 of the Limitation Act provides that an application for setting aside an ex parte decree shall have to be filed within 30 days from the date of the decree where summons was duly served and within 30 days from the date of knowledge when summons was not duly served. In our case under review there is no denial of the fact of due service of summons. So, evidently this case is governed by Article 164 of the Limitation Act, which provides that the application for setting aside the ex parte decree is required to be filed within 30 days from the date of decree impugned. The application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC having not been filed within 30 days from the date of decree, it is evidently barred by limitation. But, unfortunately, the learned Assistant Judge has allowed the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 13 CPC completely ignoring this vital aspect of the case and the law bearing on the subject. Since, on the face of the record it is evident that the application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC is barred by limitation under Article 164 of the Limitation Act and the Court has not lawfully condoned the said delay on cogent grounds, the learned Assistant Judge clearly erred in law in passing the impugned order.</u>

10. It is well settled that once a party receives an intimation of an action in a Court, it is for him to pursue it diligently and to keep himself in touch with the proceedings, either personally or through his Counsel, and the consequences flowing from his failure to keep pace with the developments must be borne by him. In the instant case, the defendant opposite party No. 2 Sher Mohammad admittedly received summons, duly filed written statement in the suit and obtained a number of adjournments and, as such, it was incumbent upon them to pursue the proceedings of the suit with due diligence. It is evident from the impugned order that defendant opposite party No. 2 Sher Mohammad did not take any step in the suit since 12-6-88 and the impugned decree was passed on 28-9-89. Under such circumstances, he must bear the whole brunt of the ominous consequences that naturally flow from his failure to keep pace with the developments of the suit, unless the failure is lawfully condoned on convincing grounds but, unfortunately, for him nothing has been done in this regard to salvage him from the inevitable legal impediments.

<u>11. Mr Mir Moklesur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, has referred me to the case of Netai Sikari and others rs, Sashi Bhusan Biswas and others, reported in 13 DLR 225,the case of Zohara Begum vs. Rafiqul Kader, reported in 25 DLR 91, the case of AK Agencies vs. Hasina Noor and others, reported in 25 DLR 250 and the case of Mian Kamal Din vs. Malik Muhammad Basher and others, reported in PLD 1952, Lahote 456 in support of his contention. In all these cases it has been consistently held that in a suit where summons has been duly served upon the defendants and they made their appearance in response to it but subsequently failed to appear and ex parte decree was passed against them, their application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC must be filed within 30 days from the date of the exparte decree and not from the knowledge of such decree. I am in respectful agreement with the principle of law laid down by the superior Courts of the Sub-continent and I must hold that Miscellaneous Case No. 106 of 1989 is barred by limitation.</u>

12. The grievance of the learned Advocate that the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in failing to discuss and consider the evidence of the witnesses of the contending parties in accordance with the correct principle of law relating to the application of evidence does not appear to be without substance. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, I hold that the learned Assistant Judge also erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and order without following the correct principle relating to the appreciation of the evidence on record.

13. For the reasons stated above, I am inclined to hold that the learned Assistant Judge seriously erred in law in passing the impugned order without properly applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. In the result, the Rule succeeds.

14. The Rule is thus made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 8-6-92 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka is set aside and Miscellaneous Case No. 106 of 1989 is dismissed.

The order or stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

Send down the LC records at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mahmudul Islam, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
Md Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate -----For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Mazharul Haque Quraishi ------ Petitioner
vs
Giridhari Rishi and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This application appears to be out of time by 399 days. The explanation for delay is that the petitioner wrongly filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 80 of 1994 before the District Judge, Dhaka against the impugned order dated 28-3-94.The petitioner invoked the application of section 14 of the Limitation Act due to prosecuting the case in a wrong forum out of bonafide mistake. Heard the learned Advocates of the parties on the point. The explanation for delay furnished in the case appears to be reasonable and acceptable and consequently the delay of 399 days in presenting the petition before this Court is condoned and the Rule is taken up for disposal on merit.

2. This Rule is directed against the order dated 28-3-94 passed by the Assistant Judge, Savar in the District of Dhaka in Title Suit No. 10 of 1994, rejecting the petitioner's application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

3. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that the mother of the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 1036 of 1995, for partition of the suit property by metes and bounds. Subsequently the said suit was transferred to the court of the Subordinate Judge (Arbitration), Dhaka and the same was renumbered as Title Suit No. 189 of 1992.

Opposite party Nos. 1-5 thereafter filed a suit in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Savar against the present petitioner and others praying for a declaration that sale deed No. 1950 dated 18-2-59 is void and inoperative by which the present petitioner or his mother did not acquire any interest in the land sold.

4. The petitioner appeared in Title Suit No. 10 of 1994 before the Assistant Judge, Savar and filed an application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for staying all further proceedings of the suit till the disposal of the aforesaid Title Suit No. 189 of 1992 before the Subordinate Judge (Arbitration), Dhaka on the ground inter alia that the main issue involved in Title Suit No. 10 of 1994 is directly and substantially in issue in Title Suit No.189 of 1992.

5. The plaintiff opposite party resisted the said application by filing written objection stating that the issues involving in the two suits are not the same and the parties of the two suits are also different and consequently section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no manner of application to the present case.

The learned Assistant Judge by his impugned order dated 28-3-94 rejected the petitioner's application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure holding inter alia that the issues involved in the two suits are not directly and substantially the same. The learned Assistant Judge further found that the parties to the two suits are also different and the two suits are of different nature, one being a simple suit for partition and the other one being for a declaration that the disputed sale deed is illegal, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned order, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, submits that the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order holding that the issues involved in the two suits are not directly and substantially the same and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr. Islam further submits that the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in holding that the parties of the two proceedings were different although, in fact, the principal contenders of the suits are practically the same and the same has occasioned failure of justice.

7. Mr. Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for plaintiff-opposite party No. 4, on the other hand, submits that the issues involved in the Partition No. 1819 of 1992 before the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and the issues involved in Title Suit No. 10 of 1994 before the Assistant Judge, Savar are quite different and as such the learned Assistant Judge was perfectly justified in rejecting the petitioner's application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Counsel further submits that in view of the fact that most of the parties in Title Suit No. 189 of 1992 are not parties in Title Suit No. 10 of 1994, the learned Assistant Judge rightly found that the parties of the two proceedings are different and consequently the impugned order does not suffer from any illegality calling for interference by this Court exercising revisional power.

<u>8. The learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner has placed before me the impugned order as well as the application under Order 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure as well as the written objection filed thereto by the contesting opposite party. Mr. Islam has placed before me the case of Sakhawat Hossain vs Chowdhury Muhammad Sarwar and another, reported in PW (Dhaka) 1968 at page 557 in support of his submission. In this case, it has been held that the essential ingredients of section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure are that both the suits are to be between the same parties or between the parties under whom they are litigating under the same title and that the matter in issue in the earlier suit is identical with the matter in issue in the subsequenti suit. Mr. Islam next cites before me the case of Fazlul Khan vs Agrani Bank and others, reported in 45 DLR 375 in which it has been held that the matter in issue in the previously instituted suit and the subsequent suit is the material consideration for success of an application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Mr. Islam then cites before me the case of Shorab Merwanji Modi and another vs Mansata Film Distributors and another, reported in AIR 1957,Cal page 727 wherein a similar view was taken.</u>

<u>9. There is no dispute to the proposition of law enunciated in the aforesaid decisions. The crucial consideration for deciding an application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is whether the matter in issue in the previously instituted suit between the same parties or between parties under whom they or any of them claim litigating under the same title is directly and substantially in issue in the subsequent suit. In fine, all the matters in issue in the two suits should be identical and the Court cannot apply this section when some issues are common and other issues are different. In our case under review, it has been found by the learned Assistant Judge that the issues involved in the two suits and the parties thereto are different. This finding of the learned Assistant Judge appears to be well-supported by the materials on record, The facts and circumstances of the present case being distinguishable from the facts of the cited cases, these are of no assistance to the petitioner</u>

<u>10. Mr. Khurshed Alam Khan on the other hand, has placed before me the case of Abdur Razzaque Dhali and another vs. Hajee Ashrafun Nessa and others, reported in 37DLR 271 in which a Division Bench of this Court considered at length the scope of section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and held that all the matters in issue in the two suits should be identical.</u>

11. In our case under consideration Title Suit No. 189 of 1992 pending before the Subordinate Judge (Arbitration), Dhaka in a suit for partition simpliciter involving 46 defendants, while Title Suit No. 10 of 1994 before the Assistant Judge, Savar is for a declaration that sale deed No. 1950 dated 18- 2-1959 is void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs, in which there are only 5 defendants, including present defendants. It is clearly found that the learned Assistant Judge was thus perfectily justified in finding that the matters in issue involved in the two suits and the parties thereto are different. In the facts and circumstances and the materials on record I hold that the impugned order does not suffer from any illegality or legal infirmity that may call for interference by this Court exercising revisional power under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

12. In view of the grievance of the petitioner that he will be prejudiced if Title Suit No. 10 of 1994 of the Court of the Assistant Judge, Savar is disposed of before the disposal of Title Suit No. 189 of 1992 pending before the Subordinate Judge (Arbitration), Dhaka deciding an important issue regarding the genuineness or otherwise of the disputed sale deed dated 18-2-59, a bone of contention in both of the suits, the petitioner, if so advised, may file an application before the proper Court for analogous or simultaneous trial of the two suits and the Court concerned will dispose of the said application on its own merit, which course is usually adopted by the Courts for avoiding any possible conflict of decision.

13. For the reasons stated above, I do not find any substance in this revision and the same accordingly fails.

14. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

The order of stay earlier granted by this Court stands vacated.

End.

lawyer:
S A M Mahbub Elahi with Md. Mizanur Rahman Bhuiyan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
No one appears ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Gulshan Ara Begum alias Jahanara and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Moazzen Hossain Chowdhury and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque J: In this Rule issued under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are directed to show cause as to why the order No. 78 dated 9.3.89 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1987 rejecting an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 95 of 1982 should not be set aside.

2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule arc that the Opposite Party Nos. I and 2 as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid Title Suit No. 95 of 1982 in the 1st Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on 3rd March, 1982 for partition of the suit land impleading Moazzem Hossain Chowdhury as defendant No. 1. This Moazzem Hossain Chowdhury is the predecessor-in-interest of the present petitioner Nos. 1-5. During pendency of the suit the defendant No. 1 died before filing written statement and the present petitioners were substituted as defendant Nos. 1(a) to 1(e) by an order dated 6.1.86 on an application for substitution filed by the plaintiffs. However, the aforesaid suit was decreed ex parte in preliminary form on 29.1.87. It is alleged by the petitioners that they were not at all aware of the aforesaid suit or of the ex parte decree passed on 29.1.87. After coming-to know of the ex parte decree they filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 25.5.87 alleging, inter alia, that the summons were not served upon them after the application for substitution was allowed by the Court.

3. It. is their case that on 21.4.87 they first came to know from plaintiff No. 2 Moazzem Hossain Chowdhury that the plaintiffs obtained a decree for partition in the court. Thereafter the petitioner No. 3 came to Court on 22.4.87 and enquired about this ex parte decree. Then he filed an application for certified copies of the impugned decree and other necessary papers on 22.4.87. He got the certified copy of the decree on 26.4.87 and then an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed before the Court on 25.5.87 which is, according to them, very much within the statutory period of 30 days to file an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in paragraphs 4 and 8 the petitioners categorically stated that the summons were not served upon them and for that reason they were not aware of the aforesaid suit or the date of hearing of the suit. They further asserted that they filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure within the statutory period from the date of their knowledge. This application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 61 of 1987.

4. From the records it appears that the notices were served upon the opposite parties about the aforesaid miscellaneous case. Opposite parties appeared before the Court on 15.2.89 and filed an application praying for time for filing written objection and the time was given upto 22.2.89 for filing written objection. But ultimately the, opposite parties did not appear and file any written objection. So the Miscellaneous Case was heard ex parte and dismissed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka on 9.3.81 after hearing the present petitioner. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 9.3.89 the petitioners preferred this revisional application and obtained the present Rule.

5. This Rule is not opposed and the assertions made by the petitioners in this application have not been challenged by the opposite parties.

6. Mr. S A M Mahbub Elahi, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that in the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure the petitioners have asserted that the application was filed within statutory period and that he did not receive any notice whatsoever about the Title Suit No. 95 of 1982 after the death of their predecessor-in-interest defendant No. 1. Mr. Elahi submits that ex parte decree was passed on 29.1.87 but the petitioners were not aware of the hearing date of the suit. On 21.4.87 they came to know about the aforesaid decree from one of the opposite parties. Thereafter on 22.4.87 they went to the Court, enquired into the matter and found that the ex parte decree was passed on 21.9.87. On the same day they filed an application for certified copy of the aforesaid decree which they got on 26.4.87. Mr. Elahi submits that if these 5 days arc deducted, then the application is found very much within time, that is, within 30 days from the date of their knowledge. The learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned order dismissed the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure holding that the ex pane decree was passed on 21.4.87 and the instant Miscellaneous Case was filed on 25.5.87 and as such it was time barred. The learned Subordinate Judge has not at all considered the fact that it took 5 days in between to obtain the certified copies of the ex pane decree and other papers. If the time is calculated from 21.4.87 to 25.5.87, after excluding the time taken for obtaining the certified copies, it clearly appears that the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed within the statutory period. So, we find that the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in computing the period of limitation in the present case. The learned Subordinate Judge further held that there was no separate application for condonation of delay in filing the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This finding is of no substance in view of the fact that we have already held that the application was filed within statutory period of limitation.

7. It is unfortunate that though there is specific allegation that the petitioners were not served with notice about the Title Suit No. 95 of 1982, the learned Subordinate Judge has not considered this aspect at all and given his finding in this respect. He ought to have considered the records in order to decide as to whether the notices were duly served upon the present petitioners after they were substituted in the aforesaid suit. Since we are in seisin of the entire records we cannot be oblivious of certain facts which are relevant for the purpose of deciding the main issue in the present proceeding. The application for substitution was allowed on 6.1.86 and thereafter the court directed the plaintiffs to serve the notice upon the substituted heirs of the deceased defendant No. 1. From the order dated 10.9.86 it appears that the summons returned unserved as per peon's report and the court directed to re-issue the summons. Order dated 30.9.86 runs as follows :

"Plaintiff filed hajira, Summons received duly served as per peon's report. So 29.1.87 for ex parte."

8. Record shows that summons were allegedly served upon the petitioners by hanging on 28.9.86 and the process server submitted report on 29.9.86, 30.9.86 was fixed in the summons for appearance of the substituted defendants. On 30.9.86 an order was passed fixing 29.1.87 for ex pane hearing. Process server has written names of two persons showing them as witnesses for service of summons. But the alleged two witnesses did not put their signatures on the summons. No summons were issued under registered post. From the above it appears that the fixing of ex pane hearing date on 29.1.87 by an order dated 30.9.86 is contrary to the provisions of Order 9 rule 6(c) of the Code of Civil Procedure which finds support from the case of M/s. Adamjee Jute Mills Ltd. Vs. Chairman, 3rd Labour Court, 1988 BLD page 1. Further, the provisions of Order 5 rule 9B of the Code of Civil Procedure have not been complied with as no summons were issued upon the petitioners by registered post with A/D.

9. On 29.1.87 PW Moazzem Hossain Chowdhury was examined and thereafter the ex parte decree was passed on the same date, that is, on 29.1.87. Now from the orders dated 30.9.86 and 29.1.87 it appears that just after the alleged service of notice by hanging next date was fixed for ex pane hearing of the suit without affording any opportunity to the present petitioners to file any written statement. It is the specific case of the present petitioners that though they were substituted they were not at all aware of the date of hearing of Title Suit No. 95 of 1982. So, the learned Subordinate Judge in fact committed an error of law in not deciding this aspect as to whether the notices were duly served upon the present petitioners before fixing date for ex pane hearing. But from the order sheet it clearly appears to us that though the notices were shown to have been served upon the present petitioners by hanging in fact they had not been given any reasonable opportunity to defend their case in view of the fact that just after the alleged service of notice, the ex pane hearing date was fixed and on that date ex parte decree was passed.

<u>10. The learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in not fixing any date for taking steps by the substituted heirs of the defendant No. 1 who admittedly died before filing any written statement. In a case like this we are of the view that the learned Subordinate Judge, before fixing the suit for ex parte hearing, must satisfy itself that the notices were duly served upon the substituted heirs but no such satisfaction has been recorded in the order dated 30.9.86. Moreover, records did not show that notices were issued both through the usual course of process server and under registered post. Our above view finds support from the case of Syed Anisul Huq Vs. MN Arif, 40 DLR 314. It is a partition suit and the decree passed in such a hot haste just after alleged service of notice cannot be sustained in law.</u>

<u>11. In that view of the matter we hold that the summons were not duly served upon the petitioners in accordance with law and the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in his decision resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 61 of 1987 and rejecting the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the above circumstances we feel that ends of justice will be met, if we set aside the ex parte decree dated 29.1.87 and restore the original suit to its file and number.</u>

12. In the result, this Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 9.3.89 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 61 of 1987 is set aside, the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is allowed, ex parte decree dated 29.1.87 is set aside and the Title Suit No. 95 of 1988 is restored to its file and number.

13. The learned Subordinate Judge is directed to hear and dispose of the aforesaid Title Suit No. 96 of 1982 in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible after giving due notices to the parties concerned.

Let the lower Court's records be sent down at once.

End.

lawyer:
AK Badrul Huq, Advocate  ------ For the Respondent No.8 Petitioner. 
NH Khandker, Advocate ------ For the Respondent No.1 Opposite Party.
parties:
Bangladesh ------ Petitioner 
VS 
Waker Ahmed and others ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md. Ansar Ali J: This is an application by defendant respondent No. 8 praying for stay of further proceedings of the Execution Case No.3 of 1993 pending in the Court of the Additional Subordinate Judge, Dhaka arising out of the judgment and decree dated 28.4.93 passed in Title Suit No.17 of 1992 by the same Court out of which First Appeal No. 73 of 1994 preferred by the defendant Government defendant No.1 and another is pending in this Court

2. Facts stated in the application in short are that respondent No. 3 as plaintiff on 11.7.85 instituted a suit in the Court of the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against the present defendant petitioner and others for declaration that the suit-property described in the schedule of the plaint belongs to the plaintiff but the same was illegally declared as abandoned property in spite of the fact that the plaintiff was always within this country even during liberation war of Bangladesh and possessing the suit-land through his tenants. The suit thereafter was transferred to the Court of Additional Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No.17 of 1992. The defendant No.9 the present petitioner filed a written statement to contest the suit and the other defendants including the Government also filed written statement to contest the same. The plaintiff examined one witness and filed some documents in support of his title but the said defendants did not adduce any evidence. The trial Court on conclusion of the trial of the suit after hearing both sides decreed the same on contest by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.4.93 and declared title of the plaintiff-respondent No. 3 in the suit-land and also granted relief for recovery of possession on the basis of the amendment of the plaint by the plaintiff vide court's order dated 29.4.92 during trial. Thereafter the decree-holder plaintiff respondent No. 3 put the impugned decree into execution by starting Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1993 in the said court of the Additional Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. But meanwhile defendant Nos. 1 and 2 preferred an appeal against the impugned judgment and decree in this court along with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 120 days and the same came up for hearing before a division bench of this Court which was pleased to condone the delay without issuing any Rule or hearing the other side with an observation that the plaintiff-respondent may however put up any objection against the condonation of delay at the time of hearing of the appeal. The appeal was accordingly registered and numbered as First Appeal No.73 of 1994 which is now pending in this court. This defendant No.9 petitioner did not however file any appeal against the impugned judgment and decree but he has been made defendant respondent No. 8 in the said appeal preferred by defendant Nos. 1 and 2. After the registration of the appeal, the defendant-appellants filed an application for stay of further proceedings of the execution case pending in the court of the Additional Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and the said application was heard by a Division Bench of this court which was pleased to stay all further proceeding of the Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1993 for a period of six months by an order dated 19.4.94. That stay order however expired on 19.10.94 but no attempt was made by the defendant-appellants for extension of the said order of stay granted earlier. Now, it appears that the defendants-appellants have filed another application for a fresh order of stay of the said execution proceeding. We shall however deal with the said application later on. This petitioner defendant No. 9 Respondent has not filed any appeal as stated above against the impugned judgment and decree passed against him and others but it has now come with this application dated 22.3.95 praying for stay of further proceeding of the execution case stating, inter alia, that it is an allottee of the government in respect of some portion of the suit property in the Dilkusha Commercial Area and has been possessing the same for community education on getting lease from the Ministry of Works and constructed a pucca tin shed in the said premises and also installed a modem Offset Printing Press and Packaging Unit therein and unless the further proceeding of the execution case is stayed till hearing of the appeal the defendant -petitioner may be ousted from the suit-property and in that case it will suffer irreparable loss and injury and that after coming to know about the latest position of the execution proceeding, the defendant-petitioner has now filed this application for stay.

3. A counter-affidavit has been filed against this application for stay, by the plaintiff respondent No.3 stating, inter alia, that the plaintiff-respondent is the sole owner of the suit-property and he has all along been within the country but the suit property was illegally declared as abandoned property at the instance of some interested persons and the plaintiff-respondent however departmentally prayed for release of the same from the list of abandoned properties but without any success. Thereafter he instituted the present suit but at the same time he went before the Court of Settlement for release of the suit-property from the list of abandoned properties as published in the Gazette and the Court of Settlement ultimately after hearing both the sides was pleased to allow the prayer of the plaintiff by its order dated 14.10.92. Meanwhile the suit was finally heard and decreed by the  learned Additional Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. It is further stated in the counter-affidavit that this defendant petitioner is an unauthorised occupier of a portion of the suit-property and has no legal authority to make any development or construction in the suit land and that he has no locus standi to file this application for stay of the proceeding and he will not suffer any substantial loss or injury and, as such, this belated application is liable to be rejected.

4. Mr. A K Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioner, submits that admittedly it filed a written statement in the suit but did not adduce any evidence and that it has not preferred any appeal against the impugned judgment and decree but it is very well in possession of a portion of the suit land for a pretty long time and meanwhile has made some improvements therein and it has also installed an Offset Printing Press and a Package Unit and unless all further proceedings of the Execution Case are stayed, the defendant petitioner will suffer irreparable loss and injury.

<u>5. Mr. NH Khandakar, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff respondent-opposite party, seriously contends that the defendant-petitioner having not preferred any appeal against the impugned judgment and decree, it has no locus standi to file this application for stay of further proceedings of the execution Case. Mr. AK Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate, on the other hand, submits referring to rule 4 and rule 33 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure that in view of the above rules and rule 5 the defendant-petitioner who has been made respondent in the said appeal has locus standi to me this application for stay of the further proceedings of the Execution case. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has relied on a decision in the case of Pamulapati Varadayya vs. Kommareddi Chinnappare Chinnappareddi and another reported in AIR 1956 Andhra Prodesh 64, wherein a similar question arose for consideration on the point of locus standi in the matter of filing an application for stay under rule 5 of Order 41 of the CPC by a non-appealing respondent and similar argument was advanced on behalf of the respondent-petitioner praying for stay of the Execution Case. A Single Bench of the High Court rejected the said application on the ground of locus standi. Then Letters Patent Appeal was preferred and the same was heard by a Division Bench presided over by Subba Rao CJ and it was held by their Lordships that under rule 4 of Order 41 CPC if the decree appealed from proceeds on any ground common to all the defendants, then anyone of them may appeal from the whole and the court may reverse the decree even in favour of all the defendants. The appeal therefore, in the circumstances mentioned in the provisions must be deemed to have been filed by one of the defendants on behalf of all the defendants. If so, it could reasonably be held without stretching the language that respondent No. 2 on whose behalf, the appeal also must be deemed to have been filed, could apply for stay under rule 5 of Order 41 CPC.</u>

6. Further rule 5 does not in express terms say that the application for stay shall be filed only by the appellant. It is a power conferred upon a court to make an order if it is moved in accordance with law. We think, that the power can be exercised in favour of respondent No. 2, for, by reason of the provisions of rule 4, a decree might be given even in his favour.

<u>7. From the above observation, we find that the application is maintainable by the non-appealing-defendant respondent. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides on this point and carefully examined the provisions of rules 4 and 5 of  Order 41 and also rule 33 of the same and we are in respectful agreement with the above observation of the learned Judges who delivered the above decision reported in AIR 1956 Andhra Prodesh and we hold that the defendant-non-appealing- respondent- petitioner who claims his interest through the other contesting defendant-appellants on common grounds of interest in the appeal has locus standi to file. the instant application for stay of further proceedings of the Execution Case No. 3 of 1993 pending in the Court of the Additional Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and hence the application is quite maintainable.</u>

8. Now, question arises whether the conditions as laid down in rule 5(3) of Order 41 of the Civil Procedure Code have been duly fulfilled by the applicant Rule 5(3) of Order 41 CPC read as follows:

5(3) No order for stay of execution shall be made under sub-rule (1) or sub-rule (2) unless the court making it, is satisfied;

(a) that substantial loss may result to the party applying for stay of execution unless the order is made.

(b) that the application has been made without unreasonable delay and

(c) that security has been given by the applicant for due performance of such decree or order as may ultimately be binding upon him;

9. It is the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that unless all further proceedings of the Execution case are stayed, substantial loss may result to the defendant-respondent-petitioner and his further contention is that the application has been filed without unreasonable delay after coming to know about the latest position of the Execution case So far the matter of security that may be necessary from the petitioner in case of stay of the execution proceeding is however left with the discretion of this court by the learned Advocate for the petitioner.

10. Mr. NH Khandakar, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff respondent-opposite party on the other hand submits that there is in fact no dispute over the ownership of the plaintiff-respondent in the entire suit-property including the premises occupied by this petitioner and that he has also succeeded in getting an order of release of the suit property from the list of abandoned properties from the Court of Settlement vide order dated 14.10.92 and at the same time he has been able to succeed in the suit and obtained a decree in his favour with declaration of his title and recovery of possession of the suit property. The present defendant petitioner did not however contest the suit and only filed a written statement on behalf of the other defendants who have of course preferred the appeal. The other contesting defendants also do not appear to have adduced any evidence by examining witnesses and the suit has been rightly decreed in favour of the plaintiff-respondent declaring his title and also allowing his prayer for recovery of possession by the impugned decree. But he has not been able to execute the said decree and take possession of the suit property and enjoy the fruits of his decree as yet. It is further submitted that the appeal filed by the contesting defendants appellants is out of time by 120 days. The delay of course appears to have been condoned by a Division Bench of this court subject to objection that may be raised at the hearing of the appeal.

<u>11. In such circumstances, the non-appealing defendant petitioner has now come with this belated application for stay of further proceedings of the Execution case started in the year 1993 only to harass the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party and deprive him of the enjoyment of the fruits of his decree and that this application has been filed by the defendant-respondent-petitioner without sufficient cause for the delay in filing this application and, in the facts and circumstances of the case, this delay in coming with the application for stay cannot but be said to be unreasonable without any satisfactory explanation. It is further contended by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party that the defendant respondent petitioner if at all was granted lease of the suit property situated in the Motijheel Area by the Abandoned Property Authority, then the lease could not be according to law for more than a year and there is no averment in the application for stay that the defendant petitioner has been granted renewal of his lease if any from year to year by the proper authority and further a lessee or allottee can not make any permanent structure, not to speak of any pucca construction on any abandoned premises according to law. In that view of the matter, if the defendant petitioner has made at all any construction or improvement thereon at the suit premises that must be at its own risk and for that it cannot say that if it is now dispossessed from the suit-premises in execution of the decree, it will suffer any substantial loss or injury. It is further contended by the learned Advocate of the plaintiff-opposite party that the defendant-petitioner has not been able to satisfy the conditions as laid down in rule 5(3) of Order 41 of the CPC and hence his application is liable to be rejected. We have considered the above submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the application and the counter affidavit and examined the relevant provisions of law and we are of the view that the defendant-petitioner has locus standi to file the application for stay but the same has been filed with unreasonable delay and such inordinate delay has not been satisfactorily explained by the petitioner.</u>

<u>12.  We therefore hold that it is not a fit case for granting stay of the further proceeding of the above execution case at this stage on this belated application of the defendant-respondent-petitioner.</u>

<u>The application is accordingly rejected.</u>

End.
